etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish یوغورت (yoğurt).

definitions.definition: A milk-based product stiffened by a bacterium-aided curdling process, and sometimes mixed with fruit or other flavoring.

quote.citation: 2009 January 24, Corey Mintz, “Lunching well at Forte bistro and lounge”, in Toronto Star‎[1]:
quote.text: Moroccan curried crab and streaks of minty, lemony yogurt add luxury to a supersimple zucchini soup ($14).

quote.citation: 2024 September 5, Alice Callahan, “Are Some Ultraprocessed Foods Worse Than Others?”, in The New York Times‎[2]:
quote.text: It makes up an estimated 73 percent of the U.S. food supply, and contains stereotypically “unhealthy” products like sodas, candies and hot dogs as well as seemingly “healthy” ones like whole grain breads, breakfast cereals, flavored yogurts and plant milks.

definitions.definition: (especially in compounds) Any similar product based on other substances (e.g. soy yogurt).
